panels.title: Shards Up
panels.description: KMS instances reporting `up` for the selected shard(s). Healthy = the full expected instance count; red at 0 means the metadata authority for that namespace shard is offline.

panels.title: Total Errors (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative KMS RPC errors since process start for the selection. Healthy = 0 (green); any non-zero turns red — see the Object RPC Totals row to pin the failing rpc.

panels.title: BeginObject rate (ops/s)
panels.description: Current-path merged-begin RPC rate — the front door of every decentralized object write. This should track the client PUT rate; if it is zero while writes flow, traffic is going through the legacy window path (see the collapsed legacy row).

panels.title: Commit rate — all flavors (ops/s)
panels.description: Combined rate of the three current-path commit RPCs (commit_object + commit_object_segmented + multi_commit_object). In steady state commits ≈ begins; a persistent gap means writes are being abandoned between begin and commit (watch write leases reaped).

panels.title: Commit fence rejects (cumulative)
panels.description: Commits rejected because the object version was already reclaimed by the orphan-version reaper (keinfs_kms_commit_rejected_version_reclaimed). Must be 0 — any non-zero means a slow writer raced the reaper; pair with keinfs_kst_committed_slot_write_rejections on the KST side.

panels.title: Write leases reaped (cumulative)
panels.description: Current-era write leases reclaimed by the sweeper because the client never committed or renewed (the successor of the legacy expired-write-intents counter). A few are normal churn; steady growth means clients abandon writes after BeginObject.

panels.title: Orphan-version backlog
panels.description: Live gauge of orphaned object versions awaiting the orphan-version reaper. Should hover near 0; sustained growth means reclaim is falling behind write churn and space is leaking until the reaper catches up.

panels.title: Current write path — BeginObject (merged begin, one txn)
BeginObject request & error rate (ops/s)
panels.description: Rate of begin_object requests and errors. This is the single pre-data control RPC of the decentralized write path (bucket/profile resolve + computed placement + lease, one FDB txn). Errors should be flat zero; the request rate is the object-write admission rate.

panels.title: BeginObject RPC latency (µs) — p50 / p99 / max (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: End-to-end begin_object latency. p50/p99 are pow2-bucketed approximations (quantized to power-of-2 steps); max (quantile=1.0) is exact. This RPC bounds the client's control-setup wall before any data moves — if it climbs, check the phase breakdown below to see whether FDB (store_begin_resolved) or a cold cache is at fault.

panels.title: BeginObject phase latency p99 (µs) — decode → resolve → route → store (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: Full p99 decomposition of the begin_object handler: request decode, bucket-context load, key normalize, profile select/validate, storage-class routing (write_profile_class_route = the small-object→replicated-profile decision), object-parent resolution, and the FDB-backed store_begin_resolved txn. Healthy: everything except store_begin_resolved sits at single-digit µs; store_begin_resolved (the one FDB txn) dominates. p99 values are pow2-bucketed approximations.

panels.title: BeginObject phase budget (last p99, µs, pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: Where the p99 µs of a begin_object call go right now. Healthy: the store_begin_resolved bar (the single FDB txn) is the only one of consequence; any other bar growing past tens of µs means a cache or resolution step regressed.

panels.title: Metadata Caches — bucket-context / ec-profile-catalog / object-parent (p99 µs)
Metadata-cache phase latency p99 (µs) — hit vs miss vs load (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: The begin-path metadata caches: bucket-context, ec-profile-catalog, and object-parent, each showing hit, miss, and (where present) load. Filter covers both rpc generations (begin_object current, initiate_object_write legacy) so the panel works whichever pipeline serves traffic. Healthy = hit phases at ~1µs and miss/load phases idle; a busy miss/load line means a cache is cold or thrashing on a hot bucket/profile.

panels.title: Key / profile resolution phase latency p99 (µs, pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: Per-request resolution steps on the begin path: key normalize, profile select/validate, the cached EC-profile list, and the storage-class routing outcomes (write_profile_default vs write_profile_alternate = small-object replicated route). Filter covers both rpc generations. All should be sub-µs to a few µs; a climbing profile_validate suggests an expensive EC-profile binding check.

panels.title: Current write path — Commit family (commit_object / commit_object_segmented / multi_commit_object)
Commit request rate by flavor (ops/s)
panels.description: Per-flavor commit rate: commit_object (single-shot small objects), commit_object_segmented (streamed large objects, long-lived), multi_commit_object (batched cross-object flush). The mix tells you the workload shape — a shift from single-shot to segmented means object sizes grew past the single-txn threshold.

panels.title: Commit latency p99 by flavor (µs, pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: Per-flavor commit p99. Do NOT read these on one mental scale: single-shot commit_object is µs-to-ms, while commit_object_segmented spans the whole streamed upload (can be minutes by design) — compare each flavor only against its own history. Values are pow2-bucketed approximations.

panels.title: Commit store-phase latency p99 (µs) — single-shot / multi / segmented internals (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: The FDB-backed store phases that separate the commit flavors internally: store_commit_object_single_shot (one txn), store_multi_commit_object (batched flush), and append_manifest_segments + seal_object (the segmented stream's per-append and final-seal txns). This is the true metadata-durability cost of each flavor; on a healthy FDB these sit in the low-ms range.

panels.title: Read path — resolve read-cache & route cache
Read-cache phase latency p99 (µs) — hit / miss / store (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: The resolve_object_read fast path: read_cache_hit should carry nearly all traffic at ~1µs; read_cache_miss + read_cache_store light up on cold objects and after invalidations. The invalidate_* phases (event-driven, matched by phase name since they are not tied to the resolve rpc) show invalidation churn — writes to hot objects. A miss-dominated picture means invalidation churn or a too-small read cache.

panels.title: Read resolve request rate (ops/s)
panels.description: Read-resolve demand: resolve_object_read (full resolve) vs resolve_object_head (the decentralized head-only resolve). Together this is the KMS-side read-metadata load; resolve rate well below client GET rate means the KSC-side resolve cache is absorbing reads.

panels.title: Route cache & discovery activity (per-second)
panels.description: Route-cache hits/misses and the route-discovery lookups/RPCs they trigger on a miss. Healthy = hits dominate; discovery RPCs are an expensive cold-path, so a steady stream of them means routes aren't sticking in cache.

panels.title: Route Cache Hit %
panels.description: Route-cache hit ratio (hits / (hits+misses)). Healthy ≥ 99% (green) once the route table has warmed; a low ratio means repeated discovery RPCs on the object-write begin path.

panels.title: Discovery RPCs (cumulative)
panels.description: Cumulative route-discovery RPCs issued on route-cache misses since process start. Should plateau once routes are warm; a continuously rising count signals route churn or a too-small route cache.

panels.title: resolve_object_read / resolve_object_head latency p99 (µs, pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: End-to-end read-resolve latency for both resolve flavors (full resolve vs decentralized head-only). A cache-hit-dominated workload keeps p99 in low µs; sustained ms-range p99 means resolves are falling through to FDB. Values are pow2-bucketed approximations.

panels.title: Background reclaim activity (per-second) — sweeper runs / leases reaped / orphan versions
panels.description: Current-era background reclaim: sweeper runs/s is the tick rate; write leases reaped/s is abandoned writes being cleaned; orphan versions reaped/s and reap errors/s are the orphan-version reaper. Healthy = steady run rate, near-zero reaps, zero reap errors. Rising lease reaps mean clients abandon writes after BeginObject.

panels.title: Background sweeper latency (avg µs)
panels.description: Average duration of a sweeper run. Should stay flat and small; a climbing run latency means the sweep is scanning more outstanding leases/versions than usual — check the orphan-version backlog stat in the vitals row.

panels.title: Not yet instrumented: FDB transaction health
panels.description: Visible placeholder for the C6 export gap — no FDB client metrics exist anywhere in the KMS tree.

options.content: **Missing [pending C6]:** the KMS FoundationDB client (multi-threaded, commit 61ba0a1) exposes **no** transaction-health metrics — no FDB commit latency, no conflict/retry counter, no transaction-too-old counter. Until instrumented, the only visibility into FDB behavior is the indirect `store_*` phase latencies above. If `store_begin_resolved` or the commit store phases spike with no KMS-side cause, suspect FDB — but there is currently no metric to confirm it. Track: code instrumentation in `poc/kms`, then keinexport export, then panels in this row.

panels.title: Object RPC Totals — request / error / latency (current + legacy generations)
Object RPC request rate (ops/s)
panels.description: Per-rpc request rate across BOTH pipeline generations. Current path: begin_object, commit_object(+segmented/multi), resolve_object_read/head, forfeit_object_write, renew_write_lease, repair_object_write, delete_object, delete_namespace_entry. Legacy window path: initiate_object_write, commit_object_write(_window). If any legacy line carries traffic, the deployment is not fully on the decentralized path.

panels.title: Object RPC error rate (errors/s)
panels.description: Per-rpc error rate for the object control-plane calls (both generations). Healthy = flat zero; any line lifting off the floor pinpoints which object operation is failing. Errors on forfeit_object_write/renew_write_lease indicate write-recovery problems, not client load.

panels.title: Object RPC total latency p99 (µs, pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: End-to-end p99 latency of each object RPC (all phases included; log scale because commit_object_segmented legitimately spans minutes while begin_object is sub-ms). Compare against the store phases in the rows above to see how much of an RPC is FDB durability vs framing. Values are pow2-bucketed approximations.

panels.title: Object RPC latency table (p50 / p95 / p99 / max, µs — pow2-bucketed approx except max)
panels.description: Latest latency percentiles per object RPC across both generations. p50/p95/p99 are pow2-bucketed approximations; the quantile=1.0 row is the exact max. Gauge cells read at a glance: green ≤ 1ms, yellow ≤ 50ms, red above — the threshold where metadata durability starts to dominate the I/O. Remember commit_object_segmented is a long-lived streaming RPC; its large values are by design.

panels.title: Reserve Shard Bypasses (cumulative, legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Reservation-cache fall-throughs to a direct allocator reserve on the initiate_object_write path. Irrelevant when traffic uses begin_object; if the legacy path still serves writes this should pin at 0.

panels.title: Reservation Cache Hit % (legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Share of reserve acquisitions served from the local stripe pool (hits / (hits+misses)). Healthy ≥ 95% when this path carries traffic; ignore when begin_object serves all writes.

panels.title: Reservation Cache Depth (legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Current depth of the in-memory reservation (stripe) pool; a depth trending toward 0 precedes bypasses. Idle/zero when begin_object serves all writes.

panels.title: Expired Write Intents (cumulative, legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Write intents reclaimed because the client never committed after initiate_object_write. The current-era counterpart is 'Write leases reaped' in the vitals row.

panels.title: Reservation Serves (cumulative, legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Lifetime reservations served from the cache to initiate calls. Pair its rate with the cache hit % to gauge pool churn on the legacy path.

panels.title: Refills (cumulative, legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Lifetime reservation-pool refills (batched stripe reservations). A spike means the pool drained faster than it refilled.

panels.title: Legacy reserve phase latency p99 (µs) — route → cache → direct reserve (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only: p99 decomposition of the reserve path inside initiate_object_write — route-resolve, cache acquire, hit/miss/wait variants, direct reserve, and the store reserve-window txn. Cache-hit phases sit at ~1µs; the wait_for_refill / direct_reserve phases only light up when the pool is starving. Empty when begin_object serves all writes.

panels.title: Legacy reserve phase budget (last p99, µs, pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Where the p99 µs of a legacy reserve go right now; wait/refill/direct bars appearing means the reservation pool is under-provisioned. Empty when begin_object serves all writes.

panels.title: Reservation cache activity (per-second, legacy)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. Rates of reservation-cache hits, misses, refills, serves, shard-bypasses, plus sweeper reservation releases. Healthy steady state on this path: serves ≈ hits, refills a low trickle, misses/bypasses/releases near zero.

panels.title: Legacy store phase totals p99 (µs) — initiate / commit / windows (pow2-bucketed approx)
panels.description: LEGACY window path only. The store_*_total FDB txn costs underneath the legacy object RPCs (initiate, reserve-window, commit, commit-window), plus queue_finalize_reservations from the legacy commit handler. Current-era store phases live in the BeginObject and Commit rows above.
